candidate.body: Office equipment has a carrying amount of ₹3,00,000 on 31 March 2021 and ₹2,00,000 on 31 March 2022. During 2021–22, equipment costing ₹30,000 was purchased, depreciation of ₹40,000 was charged, and some equipment was sold at a profit of ₹12,000. These are the only changes in the equipment balance. What cash inflow arose from the sale?
candidate.explanation: Carrying amount of the equipment sold = opening carrying amount ₹3,00,000 + purchases ₹30,000 − depreciation ₹40,000 − closing carrying amount ₹2,00,000 = ₹90,000. Sale proceeds = carrying amount ₹90,000 + profit on sale ₹12,000 = ₹1,02,000, which is the cash received from the sale (an investing inflow). ₹90,000 is only the carrying amount sold, and the other figures do not reconcile the whole movement.

candidate.body: Select the option that conveys the opposite of “negligible”, using a word from paragraph 2.
candidate.explanation: Negligible means small and not important. Paragraph 2 calls the threat monumental, meaning very big or very great, which is the opposite of small and not important. Unimpressive means not making you feel admiration or respect, exposing means putting someone at risk, and threat means the possibility that something unwanted will happen; none of these is opposite in size or importance.
candidate.passage_text:
(1) A ghost net is a fishing net lost or abandoned in the ocean. Although fishers no longer use it, it keeps working, trapping marine life. Abandoned fishing gear creates a wider problem known as ghost fishing.

(2) Ghost nets entangle turtles, dolphins, birds, sharks, seals and fish. They restrict movement, cause injuries and prevent mammals and birds from reaching air. Hundreds of animals can be caught in one net, making the threat monumental. Nets also break corals, exposing them to disease and blocking needed sunlight.

(3) Most modern nets contain nylon or other plastics that can last for centuries. Ghost nets contribute to the Great Pacific Garbage Patch. When they break down, they become smaller plastic pieces rather than disappearing. Animals mistake these microplastics for food. Eating them can harm internal organs, prevent further feeding and expose animals to toxic chemicals.

(4) Removing ghost nets requires commitment, cooperation and innovation. Conservation groups work with local fishers and governments to locate abandoned gear and remove it from the sea.

(5) Preventing abandonment also matters. Conservation organisations suggest traceable ownership so people dumping nets can be fined, and refundable deposits to encourage returning or recycling nets. Sonar reflectors can help locate lost nets. Working with small-scale fisheries can develop more sustainable gear and practices. Tackling the problem from several sides, with conservation partners, fishers and supporters, can help protect the oceans.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: For one financial year, a company has net profit after tax of ₹13,50,000, 10% debentures of ₹1,00,00,000, and a tax rate of 40%. The debentures were outstanding throughout the year and are its only interest-bearing debt. Calculate its interest coverage ratio.
candidate.explanation: Interest coverage ratio = profit before interest and tax divided by interest on long-term debt. Interest = 10% of ₹1,00,00,000 = ₹10,00,000. Profit before tax = ₹12,00,000 × 100/(100 − 40) = ₹20,00,000. Profit before interest and tax = ₹20,00,000 + ₹10,00,000 = ₹30,00,000. Ratio = ₹30,00,000 / ₹10,00,000 = 3 times. Dividing profit after tax by interest gives 1.2 and dividing profit before tax by interest gives 2, because both leave out part of the profit available to cover interest.

candidate.body: Consider the NCERT two-sector income–expenditure model, with autonomous investment and a constant marginal propensity to consume strictly between 0 and 1. Statement 1: The consumption curve is an upward-sloping straight line because consumption rises with income at a constant rate. Statement 2: The aggregate-demand curve and consumption curve are parallel. Choose the correct option.

options.text: Statement 1 is true and Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false and Statement 2 is true.

candidate.explanation: With a constant marginal propensity to consume c, consumption = autonomous consumption + cY rises with income at a constant rate, so it is an upward-sloping straight line and Statement 1 is true. In the two-sector model investment is autonomous, and aggregate demand is obtained by vertically adding that constant investment to consumption, so the aggregate demand function has the same slope c as the consumption function and the two are parallel; Statement 2 is true as well.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Course II Unit III: Determination of Income and Employment

learning_objective.why_answer_requires_it: The student must connect a constant marginal propensity to consume with the slopes of both functions.

oracle.basis: Agreed key C: first blind derivation (root developer reviewer) and second independent blind derivation (Claude Sonnet subagent (independent second reviewer)) both solved C before the official marking scheme was opened, and the official CBSE 2022-23 marking scheme maps to C (v74-official-key-comparison-v1). First: With a fixed positive MPC, consumption rises linearly with income. Autonomous investment is independent of income. Adding that constant investment shifts consumption vertically without changing its slope, so aggregate demand and consumption are parallel. Both statements are true in the explicitly named model. Second: C = C-bar + cY is an upward-sloping straight line when MPC is constant and between 0 and 1. With autonomous investment, AD = C + I-bar is a vertical shift of the consumption line, so both have slope c and are parallel. Both statements are true.

candidate.body: For one financial year, a company has net profit after tax of ₹12,00,000, 10% debentures of ₹1,00,00,000, and a tax rate of 40%. The debentures were outstanding throughout the year and are its only interest-bearing debt. Calculate its interest coverage ratio.
candidate.explanation: Interest coverage ratio = profit before interest and tax divided by interest on long-term debt. Interest = 10% of ₹1,00,00,000 = ₹10,00,000. Profit before tax = ₹12,00,000 × 100/(100 − 40) = ₹20,00,000. Profit before interest and tax = ₹20,00,000 + ₹10,00,000 = ₹30,00,000. Ratio = ₹30,00,000 / ₹10,00,000 = 3 times. Dividing profit after tax by interest gives 1.2 and dividing profit before tax by interest gives 2, because both leave out part of the profit available to cover interest.

First: Annual interest = 10000000 × 0.10 = 1000000. Profit before tax = 1200000 / (1 − 0.40) = 2000000. Profit before interest and tax = 2000000 + 1000000 = 3000000. Interest coverage = 3000000 / 1000000 = 3 times. Second: PBT = 12,00,000 x 100/60 = 20,00,000. Interest = 10% x 1,00,00,000 = 10,00,000. EBIT = 30,00,000. ICR = 30,00,000 / 10,00,000 = 3 times.

candidate.body: Albert Co. Ltd., a non-financial company, receives an insurance claim of ₹5,00,000 for machinery lost through theft. The receipt is included in net profit. When preparing cash flows by the indirect method, how should this receipt be treated?

options.text: Add it under operating activities as an extraordinary item and also subtract it from operating activities.
Subtract it under operating activities as an extraordinary item and also add it to operating activities.
Add it under operating activities as an extraordinary item and record an investing outflow.
Subtract it when adjusting operating profit for the extraordinary item and record an investing inflow.

candidate.explanation: The insurance claim for machinery lost by theft is an extraordinary item that is already included in net profit. NCERT says cash flows from extraordinary items are classified by their nature, that cash received on disposal of fixed assets is an investing inflow, and that investing incomes are deducted from net profit in the indirect method. So the receipt is subtracted when adjusting net profit to operating profit and is shown as an investing inflow, not as an outflow and not as an addition to operating activities.

Under indirect preparation, the included non-operating receipt is removed from the operating-profit calculation and the cash recovery is shown as an investing inflow. NCERT requires separately classified extraordinary cash flows according to their operating/investing/financing nature and removal of investing income from operating profit. Second: The theft insurance claim is an extraordinary gain already in net profit, so it is deducted when adjusting net profit to operating profit. Its cash effect is received against a fixed asset, so it is shown as an investing inflow. The other options pair incoherent add-and-subtract or outflow treatments.

Seeded defects carry valid learning objectives so the measured rejection is the intended defect. The two out_of_syllabus items keep the root chapter label and unit, and state their true objective.

Each seeded defect is one change to a clone of its root; explanations are deliberately left as written by the root where only the stem, key or an option changes (wrong_key, numerical_fault, missing_assumptions), as in the V73 precedent.
limitations: Two model-assisted derivations agreeing and an official key agreeing is not proof of correctness.

English contributes only two valid positives (en-q1-iv, en-q1-ix; en-q1-i is held and en-q1-v is a natural defect). The pooled English valid denominator with the regression set is 3, so one loss leaves 0.667, below the 0.70 per-subject floor.
The four English items share one 230-word stimulus, and seeded defects share a root with their positive; paired controls are correlated and this set cannot prove accuracy beyond its sample.
